newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: West Cape Maize Buyers awards yellow maize tenders.
newsitem.headline: West Cape Maize Buyers awards yellow maize tenders.

text.p: South Africa's Western Cape Maize Buyers Association said on Thursday it had awarded yellow maize tenders totalling 190,000 tonnes to a number of players for delivery from September until April 1997.
He said a second tender of 60,000 tonnes of yellow maize had been awarded to Seaboard Shipping. The tender price was 724.25 rand and was for delivery in April 1997.

The association had also purchased 95,000 tonnes of yellow maize from the state-owned Maize Board at a price of 817.17 rand a tonne, van der Merwe said. Deliveries would commence immediately, continuing until the beginning of March 1997.
Van der Merwe said the association was likely to hold more tenders for yellow maize.
"We will watch the January-February situation and might have to ask for more tenders. We will probably have to," he said.
He said although the tenders did not specify that maize be imported, it was likely traders would tap the U.S. market for maize.
"They will probably have to import. I don't think there is anything (yellow maize) available here. The U.S. is really the only place."
He said the maize specified by the association would have to be U.S. No.2 or of the same quality.
Imports could also continue into the new season, which commences in May 1997, van der Merwe said.
"There is seldom local maize available at the beginning of the season. We will probably have to import for the month of May. But it will depend on the price and the market situation," he said.

South Africa faces a yellow maize shortage of up to 700,000 tonnes this season and may be forced to import as domestic supplies have been drained by a high level of exports and large-scale deliveries to the Maize Board's export pools.
The shortage could, however, be smaller if some maize earmarked for export, notably that in the Board's pools, finds its way back onto the domestic market.
The shortage appears to be most acute in the coastal areas, such as the Western Cape province which are furthest from the central maize growing belt.

South Africa is expecting a maize crop of 9.484 million tonnes, up from 4.406 million in 1995. The crop comprises 4.044 million tonnes of yellow maize and 5.44 million tonnes of white. A surplus of white is expected this season.
